skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Five remote-installer pipe-to-shell examples are confirmed because they execute downloaded code without integrity verification. Most static matches are false positives from environment-management documentation and local examples. The helper also has confirmed secret-exposure risks when it prints differences, disables masking, or accepts passwords on the command line. Static review was capped at 400/681 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 281 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installation commands execute downloaded scripts directly.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell instructions with a version-pinned download and published checksum verification, or direct users to UV official installation documentation.
Mask values for keys containing SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, KEY, or credential URL fields by default, with an explicit confirmation for any reveal option.

remediation.issue: The no-mask template option can write live values.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the option or require an interactive confirmation and emit a warning that the result contains secrets.

remediation.issue: Passwords can be supplied in command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the password argument and accept passwords only through a secure prompt or standard input.

semantic_findings.title: Secrets may be exposed in terminal output

content.value_statement: Project configuration often mixes secrets, environment values, and deployment settings without clear safeguards. This skill provides structured guidance, templates, and helper workflows for managing them in Python projects.
actual_capabilities: Create environment variable templates for Python projects.
Validate required variables in a selected environment file.
Identify placeholder values and weak secret values.
Compare development and production environment file structures.
Generate masked configuration templates from local environment files.
Document UV and python-dotenv setup patterns.
limitations: It does not provision cloud secrets managers or rotate provider credentials.
It cannot determine whether a real secret has already been exposed.
The helper operates on local files selected by the user.
Encryption safety depends on password handling and secure storage of encrypted files.

use_cases.title: Set up a new Python project
use_cases.description: Create a committed template and local environment file rules before adding application secrets.

use_cases.title: Standardize deployment settings
use_cases.description: Compare required variables across development, staging, and production without designing a custom format.

use_cases.title: Review configuration hygiene
use_cases.description: Check a local environment file for missing values and common placeholder secrets before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic template
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a .env.template for a Python project. Include database, application, and API settings, but use placeholders only.

prompt_templates.title: Validate required settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to validate my local .env file for APP_NAME, DATABASE_URL, and SECRET_KEY without printing their values.

prompt_templates.title: Separate environments
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe development, staging, and production environment file structure for this Python service. Explain which files should be committed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit configuration workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed environment configuration workflow. Identify secret exposure risks, recommend masking rules, and provide a secure release checklist.

output_examples.input: Create a template for a Python web service.
output: A list of required environment variable names.
Placeholder values that contain no live credentials.

output_examples.input: Compare development and production configuration requirements.
output: Variables present only in each environment.
A masked summary of differing settings.
Recommended variables to validate before deployment.

output_examples.input: Check my environment file before release.
output: Warnings for placeholder or short secret values.

best_practices: Commit templates only, and exclude real environment files and secret files from version control.
Mask secret values in logs, terminal output, code review, and support tickets.
Use a managed secrets service for production credentials when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not store live credentials in example files or documentation.
Do not print complete environment differences in shared terminals or CI logs.
Do not pass passwords as command-line arguments.

faq.question: Does this skill store my secrets?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and local helper examples. You control the files and commands you run.

faq.question: Can I commit a .env file?
faq.answer: Do not commit files with real secrets. Commit a template containing variable names and safe placeholders instead.

faq.question: Does it support production secrets managers?
faq.answer: It documents configuration patterns but does not provision or operate a secrets manager.

faq.question: Can it validate required variables?
faq.answer: Yes. The included helper examples can check whether selected variable names are present.

faq.question: Will comparisons reveal secret values?
faq.answer: The included comparison helper can print differing values. Use masked output and avoid running it in shared logs.

faq.question: Is file encryption enough for production secrets?
faq.answer: No. Use strong password handling, access controls, backups, and a managed secrets service when appropriate.
